recipes.title: Create automatic subtitles
recipes.result: A reviewed subtitle file or styled subtitle timeline.
recipes.setup: AutoSubs and media containing clear speech. Check the current installer and Resolve integration requirements before use.
steps: Open an audio or video file in AutoSubs standalone mode.
Choose a transcription model and language, then transcribe.
Review the transcript, speakers and timing; export SRT or text.
For styled Resolve output, follow the provider’s Resolve integration guide and send the reviewed subtitles to Resolve.
recipes.limitations: Model downloads need a connection. Check model licenses and transcription accuracy. The provider excludes the Mac App Store Resolve build. Not installation tested by this catalogue.

sources.label: AutoSubs quick start and model licensing

alternatives.description: Style an existing subtitle file as editable Text+ clips. This covers subtitle presentation; it does not establish automatic speech recognition.

recipes.title: Explore a print-film look
recipes.result: An editable print-film treatment with a documented input and output pipeline.
recipes.setup: A Resolve project and a PowerGrade suited to its color-management pipeline. The legacy Kodak 2383 download includes Resolve 14–16 versions; current-version compatibility is not established here.
steps: Choose a PowerGrade that matches your project’s color-management workflow; compare YRGB and color-managed alternatives.
Download from the original creator and read the included instructions.
For the legacy Kodak 2383 PowerGrade, use Gallery Import and choose the extracted DPX/DRX file as described by the creator.
Apply on a duplicate grade, check exposure and skin tones, then compare bypassed and treated output. Keep input and output transforms explicit.
recipes.limitations: A film-inspired look is not a guarantee of physical film reproduction. Avoid a second display transform. No preview image is reproduced without permission; use the creator’s samples.

sources.label: Juan Melara: Kodak 2383 installation and alternatives

alternatives.description: Compare the separate DaVinci YRGB print-film collection. Match its input and color-management instructions to your project before choosing a PowerGrade.

recipes.title: Grade action-camera log footage
recipes.result: A model-matched log-to-display starting point, followed by shot correction.
recipes.setup: This example is limited to Osmo Action 5 Pro clips recorded in D-Log M and DJI’s corresponding Rec.709 vivid LUT. Other models and profiles need their own documentation.
steps: Confirm the camera model and recording profile from the shoot settings. Separate Normal, HLG and D-Log M clips.
Find the Osmo Action 5 Pro D-Log M to Rec.709 vivid LUT on DJI’s official downloads page.
Follow the Resolve color-training guide to install and apply the LUT, keeping its expected input and output explicit.
Compare a duplicate grade, adjust each shot, and check scopes and the target display. Do not apply this example to an unverified camera/profile pair.
recipes.limitations: D-Log M and D-Log are different profiles. DJI clip color organizes metadata; it does not transform pixels. This recipe is an editorial starting point, not a tested setup or an Action 6 claim.

sources.label: Blackmagic Design: color training and manuals

alternatives.title: Leeming LUT Pro 4 for Osmo Action 5 Pro
alternatives.description: A paid, camera-specific alternative. Its Action 5 Pro guide specifies its own capture and white-balance workflow and Rec.709 gamma 2.4 target. Use the corresponding Leeming LUT and its instructions; the DJI LUT steps above do not establish that workflow. This catalogue has not compared the results.
